title: It's a bit counterintuitive. But the players that are "better in Best Ball" are typically the boring guys. Merely getting volume every week is worth tons in that format. If a player turns out to be a zero in season-long format, it's not end of world. We just cut and grind the waiver wire. Travis Hunter a classic example: * If you draft him in Best Ball and he runs 5-10 routes/game all season, it's horrible for your team EV * If you draft him in season-long and he has a bit WR role, simply replace him with something hot off the wire
